transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-07
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood Product), Mike (Bluebridge CTO), Lisa (Lead ML Eng), Arjun (Infra)

Summary:
Quick product walkthrough focused on selecting open models from the catalog, reading compatibility matrices, interpreting bench signals, and where Redwood Optimize suggests quantization or batching guardrails. Customer wants a realistic bench and an apples-to-apples latency/cost comparison for hosted vs dedicated.

Topics covered:
- Catalog filters and compatibility flags
- Bench configuration and fidelity (tokens, context length)
- Routing/fallbacks for constrained capacity
- Optimize recommendations: batching, KV caching, quant profiles
- Security and deployment options (hosted/dedicated/private)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Sofia: okay hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sofia from Redwood, real quick intros?
[00:08] Mike: yeah hey Mike Chen here CTO at Bluebridge - thanks for doing this demo.
[00:12] Lisa: Lisa Park, lead ML eng, we'll be owning the bench and prompt set.
[00:15] Arjun: Arjun, infra - i'll be looking at VPC and network stuff.
[00:19] Daniel: Daniel Kim, solutions engineer at Redwood, i'll drive the catalog and the bench walkthrough.
[00:23] Priya: Priya Nair, product, i'll show Optimize suggestions near the end.
[00:27] Sofia: great, bought up the agenda, we'll do a short qualification then jump into the console and the model catalog, run a quick compatibility lookup and then sketch a bench plan.

[02:05] Sofia: Mike, quick question on constraints — is the priority latency or cost for your chat assistant?
[02:12] Mike: it's kind of both, we want sub-200ms for short replies but cost matters, we're currently paying around $0.015 per 1k tokens with our current provider and want to beat that with comparable quality.
[02:25] Lisa: and our context windows are typically 2k tokens, sometimes longer for docs flow so compatibility with 4k+ models would be nice.

[03:10] Daniel: okay, on the catalog side we'll filter by architecture and quantization readiness, then look at the compatibility matrix which shows kernel availability per hardware. quick note the catalog sometimes calls kv cache as "KV cash" in older we exported, ignore that typo.
[03:28] Lisa: ha okay noted. also we have strict requirements around caching because we do few-shot with repeated prefixes.

[05:00] Daniel: opening the Console -> Models tab now. first column is model family, second is version, then runtime hints: recommended kernel (e.g., flash-attn2), quantization status (int8, q4_0, q5), memory footprint, and a compatibility badge per device class.
[05:22] Daniel: if i search for open-models and filter for "4k+ seq" and "quant-ready" we get a shortlist: osm-3-small, emma-13b-v2-q4, lucerne-7b-4k.
[05:35] Lisa: hmm emma-13b seems promising, but what's the bench signal for hallucination on instruction-tuned tasks?

[06:12] Daniel: good question. the bench panel shows our curated evals: instruction-following score, hallucination rate, and latency at 8 and 16 batch sizes. emma-13b has strong instr-follow but a slightly higher hallucination on long docs. we surface that as a red flag on the compatibility matrix under "eval drift".

[07:40] Mike: can you explain how the compatibility matrix maps to our on-prem hardware? we run A100 80GB and some T4s for inference.
[07:50] Daniel: yes, the matrix rows are models, columns devices; cells show kernel maturity: green=optimized kernel available, yellow=experimental, gray=no kernel yet. for A100 80GB emma-13b shows green for fp16 + q4_0 path. for T4 it's yellow, meaning we can run but expect higher latency.

[09:05] Arjun: do you support private deployment with customer-managed KMS? we need CMKs for tokens at rest.
[09:12] Priya: yes we support KMS/HSM integrations, the Private package includes KMS hooks and audit logs. we'll share the SOC2 package but the initial security review should cover SAML/SSO, RBAC and key rotation cadence.

[11:00] Daniel: back to bench configuration — critical piece: we emulate your prompt patterns, context length distribution, and concurrency. artifacts we ask for: 1) sample prompts, 2) typical concurrency / qps, 3) SLOs. we run microbench (latency-only), macrobench (throughput under load), and quality evals using your prompt set.
[11:35] Lisa: we can provide a 5k prompt sample with weighting across short vs long contexts.

[13:10] Daniel: in the Console bench wizard you can pin sequence length buckets, token weights and set hardware targets — we recommend also enabling KV caching in the bench to simulate prefix reuse; Optimize will recommend cache TTL and batching window based on measured p50/p95.

[15:02] Mike: what about routing? say a model is out of capacity during spikes, will Redwood automatically fallback to a cheaper variant?
[15:12] Sofia: yes, routing policies allow priority rules: prefer low-latency variant, fallback to quantized variant if capacity constrained, and final fallback to hosted cheaper tier. you can also set quality thresholds so fallback won't be used if hallucination risk is too high.

[17:00] Lisa: can we control quantization levels per route? we don't want q4 on customer-facing flows.
[17:08] Daniel: absolutely — per-route policies allow you to pin model version and quant profile. we show this in a policy editor; i'll demo a canary where 10% traffic goes to fp16 emma-13b and 90% to q4_0 emma-13b.

[19:30] Daniel: demoing the compatibility matrix export — clicking "export CSV" and opening it. columns: model, version, device kernels, expected latency p50/p95 (from baseline bench), memory footprint, suggested quant profile, eval scores. you can upload this to your internal tools.

[21:10] Lisa: for the bench numbers, are those from Redwood's public benches or seeded with your weights? we need to know if bench uses same tokenizer and instruction templates.
[21:22] Daniel: bench uses the same tokenizer and our eval harness is open-sourced; for customer benches we run the bench on your prompts + tokenizer to ensure apples-to-apples. public benches are indicative but we always recommend the customer-run bench.

[23:05] Priya: showing Optimize suggestions now — it looks at request distribution and recommends batching window size, KV cache TTL, and quant profile prioritization. for Bluebridge's distribution it recommends a 12ms batching window and q4_0 for background generation, fp16 for low-latency critical paths.

[24:40] Mike: curious about end-to-end P99 with batching — if we batch we'll save cost but won't meet strict p99. can Optimize simulate tradeoffs?
[24:50] Priya: yes Optimize runs an SLO simulation: you input target p99 and cost cap and it recommends feasible configs. it will also suggest hybrid routing: small requests routed to low-latency pools unbatched, large requests batched into cheaper pools.

[27:30] Arjun: any gotchas with VPC peering or egress for private deployments? we have strict egress rules.
[27:38] Daniel: for Private we offer direct VPC endpoints and can lock egress to internal subnets; for Hosted we provide region locking and data retention controls. note: some older docs refer to "VPC peering keys" incorrectly — ignore that, use the endpoint IP ranges we share.

[30:12] Lisa: can we surface hallucination regressions over time? we need alerting if a rollout increases hallucination by X%.
[30:20] Priya: yes, Quality Monitoring supports regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can set thresholds and get automatic rollbacks if quality drops.

[32:00] Daniel: demoing a bench result — emma-13b on A100 80GB: p50 95ms, p95 240ms at batch=8; q4_0 path p50 80ms p95 220ms but hallucination rose 2.4 percentage points on your long-doc evals.

[34:10] Mike: curious, on cost calc where is token counting coming from? do you support custom tokenizers?
[34:20] Daniel: cost uses tokenization at inference layer; for bespoke tokenizers we can bring your tokenizer into the bench so costs reflect your tokenization.

[36:05] Lisa: can we run an A/B where we compare emma-13b vs lucerne-7b and get side-by-side metrics including hallucination and latency?
[36:12] Daniel: yes that's a standard bench — we can parameterize bench to run multiple models and produce a picklist with tradeoffs. we'll include model-quality graphs and kernel maturity notes.

[38:30] Sofia: quick question on procurement timeline — Mike, when are you planning to make a decision?
[38:36] Mike: aiming for an internal decision in about 3-4 weeks, budget signoff by end of Jan.

[39:10] Sofia: good, we'll plan a 2-week technical bench and then a security review. next steps we'll send pricing and SOC2 docs, SE team will run bench.

[40:00] Lisa: small nit: we've had issues with numeric stability when quantizing certain decoder layers; does Redwood have per-layer quant opt recommendations?
[40:12] Daniel: yes Optimize includes per-layer quant hints and identifies sensitive layers; in some cases we recommend mixed precision or selective dequant of LN ops. we'll annotate that in the bench notes.

[42:25] Arjun: about SLA — does dedicated come with latency SLOs? and what does the failover look like?
[42:33] Sofia: Dedicated has tiered SLAs; failover is policy-driven: we can burst to hosted capacity or route traffic across regions. we'll send the SLA matrix in the docs.

[44:00] Priya: closing with a short recap — deliverables: bench config & results, pricing options, security pack. Daniel will kick off the bench once Arjun shares qps and sample prompts.

[45:20] Mike: thanks all, felt like a productive session.
[45:25] Sofia: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the links and next steps.

End of transcript.
